newsitem.title: USA: Secret Service director resigns to join Ameritech.
newsitem.headline: Secret Service director resigns to join Ameritech.

text.p: The director of the U.S. Secret Service, which protects the president, vice president and their families, has resigned to join the Chicago-based telecommunications company Ameritech Corp, the White House said on Wednesday.
President Bill Clinton strongly praised the official, Eljay Bowron, and said in a statement that he accepted the resignation with regret.

"For 23 years, Eljay Bowron has focused his intelligence, judgement and deep professionalism on implementing, improving and reforming the critical national missions of the United States Secret Service," Clinton said. "He will be missed."
White House officials said they did not know whether Bowron, 46, was eligible to retire and said his decision to leave reflected a desire to spend more time with his family.
